We start with zero and one. These are our two starting values.
To make the next number, add the previous two. Then use the newest pair, and do it again.
The small labels tell us each number's place. We start at F zero, so F two is the third entry.
The older value sits on the left. The newer value sits beside it. Their labels move with them.
Listen for plus and equals. The answer appears when we say its name, and becomes our newest value.
Number windows show values, not piles of things. A window marked one thousand stands for that value, not one thousand objects.
We'll keep adding until the sequence first passes one hundred million. The numbers grow, but the rule stays the same.
